title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review initial benchmark results, confirm access and environment readiness for Redwood Private deployment, discuss tuning (batching/KV cache/quantization), and agree on next steps including security questionnaire and a production-like benchmark run.
action_items: Liam Chen - Grant Redwood cross-account IAM role for benchmarking (aws-prod-redwood-role) - due 2027-10-08
Samira Patel - Send Redwood security pack + SOC2 report and short notes about KMS integration - due 2027-10-07
Ethan Cole - Schedule 2-hour production-like benchmark run and share runbook and sample prompts - due 2027-10-11
Olivia Park - Complete initial security questionnaire and indicate data residency reqs - due 2027-10-12
Maya Rivera - Provide 3 representative prompt sets and expected SLO targets (latency, throughput) - due 2027-10-09
next_steps: Redwood to receive cross-account access and run production-like benchmark on customer infra
Redwood to share SOC2 + KMS notes and follow up on encryption-at-rest details
Customer to confirm final pod sizes and whether dedicted capacity or private on-prem is required
Schedule deep-dive next week on tuning quantization and batching after benchmark results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-06 14:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samira, Ethan, Jordan (Redwood) - Maya, Liam, Olivia, Noah (NexaHealth)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, good morning, good afternoon. quick agenda — check onboarding status, bench results we ran last night, and next steps for the private deployment.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks Samira. we got your note, we're eager to see the numbers. we also still have a couple of internal hoops for VPC peering.
00:30 Speaker 3 (Liam): yeah so on infra side we've provisioned a staging VPC and an empty eks cluster. we still need to set up the cross-account role and some egress rules.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Samira): Perfect, that was one of the asks — if you can grant the aws role (redwood-bench-role) with sts:AssumeRole we'll kick off the run. Ethan, quick summary of the bench?
00:55 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Sure. We ran the sample 1k prompt pass overnight against a small private instance you provided. Observations: median latency for 1k tokens was ~420ms per request with batching at 8 and KV caching enabled. The tokens/sec was about 185 on the instance we used. Note — transcription here: some of the names in the results sheet may look off, the export changed Redwood-verify to redwood-varify.
01:20 Speaker 3 (Liam): 420ms median is pretty good. what's the variance? we saw a long tail on one of the runs.
01:30 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Tail popped up when concurrent slots hit 12, that pushed queue wait time. When we dropped concurrency and increased batch size to 12, median increased slightly but p95 improved. There's a tradeoff. Also quantization helped reduce memory pressure — we tested 8-bit and saw about 20% cost improvement but some small quality diffs on our regen checks.
01:55 Speaker 2 (Maya): Did you try the separate model variant? We want to understand fallback behavior vs latency.
:02:05 Speaker 4 (Ethan): We did a canary with a smaller distilled model; fallback latency was lower but hallucination on structured outputs increased. Recommend primary as full model + fallback to distilled for non-critical requests.
02:25 Speaker 5 (Olivia): quick security question — how are logs handled? audit trail is important for us.
02:33 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Audit logs are available, we can ship S3-based audit export or push to your SIEM via syslog. We also hash PII in logs by default in the hosted flow; for Private we can configure KMS-managed encryption and customer-managed keys.
02:50 Speaker 5 (Olivia): Ok, we need confirmation on KMS integration and whether HSM is required for encryption keys. Also SSO/SAML mapping and RBAC details.
03:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll include a short note on KMS vs HSM in the security pack. Jordan will attach the SOC2 and the one-pager on KMS best practices.
03:18 Speaker 6 (Noah): small clarifying Q on onboarding: do you need sample data or only prompts to run the bench?
03:25 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Prompts and a small set of reference documents are enough for initial perf runs. For evals we do require a few representative records, but those can be synthetic.
03:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): On the network side, we hit one snag — our egress policy is locked down. If Redwood needs to pull images we need to whitelist certain registry domains. Can you share the list?
03:50 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, that's in the runbook. I'll paste the registry and registry IP ranges.
04:00 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Also to call out, the runtime does a lot of automatic batching and prefix KV cache reuse — sometimes the KV cash (sic) word gets misspelled in older docs, so ignore that. If you plan longer context lengths we'll tune kernel selection and sequence packing.
04:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): About quantization — you said 8-bit worked but quality drop observed. Can you quantify?
04:25 Speaker 4 (Ethan): On our sample regen test, ROUGE-style scoring dropped about 1.8 points on average for structured outputs. For free-form responses the diff was negligible. Recommend A/B on your prompts during the benchmark run.
04:40 Speaker 5 (Olivia): compliance — any third party subprocessors? we need a list for procurement.
04:48 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll include subprocessors list in the security pack — major cloud partners, monitoring provider, and encryption tooling.
04:55 Speaker 6 (Noah): timeline question: if we greenlight after this bench how long to get to a pilot?
05:03 Speaker 1 (Samira): If bench is green and access is in place, we can do a 4-week pilot. First week: integration and test runs, weeks 2-3: production-like load, week 4: handover + cost tuning.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Liam): sounds good. I'll prioritize the IAM role today.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Maya): one more — can Redwood run a data residency sim? we have EU-only reqs for certain datasets.
05:36 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Yes, we can pin region and run on EU-hosted nodes; we'll note any perf delta vs US region.
05:45 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok let's recap action items and owners — Liam will do the role, Olivia completes questionaire, Ethan runs benchmark once access granted, Samira sends security docs. We'll follow up with a 60-90 minute deep dive once bench results are in.
06:05 Speaker 2 (Maya): thanks all, appreciate it.

[End of transcript]
